subject: Performance commitment clarifications and PoC asks — p95/p99 & streaming
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@skyrise.health>, Matthew Cole <matthew.cole@skyrise.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance commitment clarifications and PoC asks — p95/p99 & streaming

Hi Elaine / Matthew — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and a short checklist so we can scope a hosted PoC that validates your p95/p99 SLOs and streaming behavior vs your current provider. Please confirm the shaded items or correct if I misunderstood.

Recap (from our call)
- Goal: Validate end-to-end user-facing latency for Skyrise chat endpoint under realistic traffic patterns. You want numeric acceptance for p95 and p99 that we can bake into the contract if the PoC validates them.
- Current provider: your internal measurements pointed to p95 ~ 480ms and p99 ~ 1.6s (end-to-end, app -> model -> app). You want improvements and predictable tail behavior.

Clarification checklist (please confirm):
1) Target SLOs to validate during PoC: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 1.0s (end-to-end, 95/99 percentiles measured at the application surface after streaming reassembly).
2) Average request size: 120 tokens (prompt + context); 95th percentile token count: 420 tokens.
3) Steady QPS: 35 QPS; burst to 320 QPS for short windows (30–90s).
4) Peak concurrent active connections: ~50 concurrent users generating streaming answers.
5) Streaming expectations: first-token latency <= 180ms; steady-state per-token latency (after first token) <= 30ms; ability to sustain ~400 tokens/s aggregate across connections without backpressure.
6) Failure/fallback policy: want automatic fallback to smaller model variant with preserved latency SLO during node maintenance.

PoC scope we propose (attached detailed plan):
- 5-day run, split across two regions (us-east1 + us-west1).
- Synthetic harness that replays real traffic profiles (we'll provide harness & instrumenting instructions).
- Measurement of end-to-end percentiles from your client-side vantage + provider-side traces.
- Network baseline: please send a recent pcap or run our packet-capture template attached.

Questions / asks from Skyrise to confirm before we schedule PoC:
- Can you confirm the token counts above?
- Do you have a hard maximum latency bar (e.g., support ticket threshold) beyond which the feature is considered degraded?
- Any regulatory constraints on telemetry we should know about (PII, redaction)?

Next steps
- If the checklist looks right, propose tentative PoC week: Oct 4–8.
- Please review the attached PoC test plan and return the packet-capture template populated by Tue 09/21.
- I’ll loop in Laura and Marcus on the engineering side after we lock the dates.

Thanks — looking forward to validating this for you.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: redwood_poc_test_plan_v1.pdf (PoC steps, metrics to capture), network-pcap-template.txt (pcap instructions)

From: Elaine Park <elaine@skyrise.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matthew Cole <matthew.cole@skyrise.health>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance commitment clarifications and PoC asks — p95/p99 & streaming

Thanks Ben — concise and helpful. Confirmations below and a couple of tweaks.

Confirmations / corrections
- Token counts: average is closer to 150 tokens; 95th percentile ~ 480 tokens. Good catch on the long tails.
- Steady QPS: 40 QPS; burst to 300 QPS (we see bursts driven by marketing campaigns).
- Peak concurrent: 48 concurrent streaming sessions on average during peaks; we can provision a small test pool up to 80 if needed.
- Streaming: first-token target 150–200ms acceptable; per-token steady-state target <= 25ms. We care about visible typing latency for live UX.
- Current provider baseline: p95 ~ 500ms, p99 ~ 1.4–1.7s depending on region.

Data / access notes
- We can provide a 3-day window of traffic capture (we'll sanitize PII) and run your packet-capture template by 09/21.
- Telemetry constraint: we cannot send raw user text off our VPC; we'll work with you to run the harness in our environment and provide anonymized traces and metrics.

PoC timeline
- Oct 4–8 looks good on our side. We prefer starting with us-east1. Please confirm the test harness requirements and any client-side dependencies.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Product, AI | Skyrise Health
elaine@skyrise.health

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance commitment clarifications and PoC asks — p95/p99 & streaming

Elaine — perfect, thanks for the quick confirmation and the extra detail on token tails. A few engineering clarifications and the explicit PoC runbook we will use.

Engineering clarifications (short):
- Telemetry approach: since you cannot export raw text, we'll run the harness inside your VPC (agentless runner) and collect anonymized timing traces + aggregated token counts. We'll provide a small script that hashes prompts locally and emits only timing samples + token counts.
- Measurement definitions: p95/p99 will be computed on end-to-end request completion time (application event emitted when stream is fully reassembled client-side). Streaming first-token latency measured as time from request start to first bytes delivered.
- Concurrency shaping: our harness can emulate up to 400 concurrent connections; for the PoC we'll run with 50/100/200 concurrency steps to show tail behavior.
- Network path: ask IT to run the attached pcap template from your closest app server to the public endpoint we give you. That will let us correlate network RTT vs server-side queueing.

Offer during PoC
- For the PoC we will standby a small hosted capacity pool configured with the same model you plan to serve. If we validate p95/p99 targets as defined, we will provide an introductory commitment credit toward the first month of Dedicated capacity. Details to follow from contracting.

Immediate asks from Skyrise for PoC kickoff
1) Confirm sanitized traffic or allow local harness.
2) Populate network-pcap-template.txt and return by 09/21.
3) Confirm PoC start date (we propose Oct 4).

I'll schedule a 30-minute engineering sync for Wed 09/22 to walk through the harness and instrumentation. Laura / Marcus — can you be on the call?

Best,
Ben

Attachments: redwood_poc_test_plan_v1.pdf, network-pcap-template.txt
